rules-note: Business strikes only, including the P and D coins the Mint sold only in rolls, bags and boxes: no proofs or reverse proofs, no Special Mint Set, special finish set or other set-only special strikes (Burnished, Enhanced Uncirculated), no silver or bullion strikes. Every coin carries a mint mark (mintMark is never null). variety is the design as displayed in the source, null where one design covers the year; a variety is listed only where the source has a separate row with its own figure, and edge-lettering errors are not varieties. Mintages come only from the saved source, null where it gives no figure; nothing is summed, split or estimated, and totals are ignored. Release order: designs in source order, then the mints. isKeyDate is false throughout because no cited source names key dates; no images. This file: the "Circulation strikes:" list of "Eisenhower dollar", 1971-1978 copper-nickel clad, P and D (no dollars are dated 1975). The Philadelphia coins carry no mint mark on the coin (infobox: "Mint mark omitted on Philadelphia Mint issues") but are "P" here, so that mintMark is never null. The 1776–1976 Bicentennial coins have separate Type I and Type II rows with their own figures, so they are the varieties "Type I" and "Type II"; every other coin has variety null. The 1972 reverse types have no figures of their own and are not varieties. Excluded: the 40% silver S coins ("Uncirculated silver:" list, including the 3-coin Bicentennial set) and every proof.
